subject: Orion AI: unexpected tail latency after model canary
body:
From: Jamie Collins <jamie@orionai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@orionai.com
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: (URGENT) Hosted API latency spike after canary

Hi Hannah,

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency for our generation traffic right after you pushed the v2.1-canary variant last night. p95 has moved from ~230ms to ~1.6s and p99 is intermittently hitting 2.8s; a few requests timed out and our client retried which amplified throughput. This started ~2026-09-05T01:40Z and is still ongoing.

Attached is a short sample of request traces and the application-side logs (orion_latency_samples.log). Can you tell us if anything changed in the canary (kernel/quantization/batching) that would explain KV cache invalidation or larger allocation spikes? This is impacting our SLA window — we need a rollback or a mitigation ASAP.

Thanks,
Jamie
Jamie Collins
Head of Platform, Orion AI

Attachments: orion_latency_samples.log (text, 47KB)

---

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Collins <jamie@orionai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 09:00:22 -0000
Subject: Re: (URGENT) Hosted API latency spike after canary

Jamie — thanks for the heads up and for the log sample. I'm escalating to SRE and runtime immediately.

Immediate plan:
- Marcus: can you triage the canary hostpool and confirm if the v2.1-canary build introduced any execution path changes?
- Priyom: please prepare a rollback plan and an ETA for routing to stable if we need to pause the canary.
- Connor: I will loop you in on communications to Orion for cadence and credits if we need to make good on SLA.

Marcus and Priyom, I am putting this at highest priority. I will update Orion within 30 minutes.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Incident Lead, Redwood Inference

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 09:23:45 -0000
Subject: Re: (URGENT) Hosted API latency spike after canary

Quick triage notes:
- Verified: tail latency increase correlates with canary rollout at 01:35Z.
- Observed: an uptick in KV cache misses for long-context requests and a higher allocation rate on the attention kernels for v2.1-canary.
- Hypothesis: the new attention kernel changes the memory access pattern; GC/arena fragmentation on those host instances causes occasional stalls for requests with >2k tokens.

I've pulled CPU and GPU-side flamegraphs and some per-request timelines; attaching profiling-flamegraphs.tar.gz and a small incident bundle (incident_logs.zip).

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Pause canary traffic and failover to stable v2.0 for affected customers (fast, low risk).
2) Apply a temporary routing policy that pins long-context requests to nodes with older kernel until we fix the kernel (higher complexity).

I recommend option 1 for Orion while we debug — I'll post a short checklist for the rollback so on-call infra can execute safely.

Attachments: profiling-flamegraphs.tar.gz (tar.gz, 9MB), incident_logs.zip (zip, 1.2MB)

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 10:05:03 -0000
Subject: Re: (URGENT) Hosted API latency spike after canary

Agree with Marcus. My recommended action: pause the v2.1 canary and route Orion's traffic back to v2.0-stable.
Planned steps (ETA ~20 minutes after approval):
- Pause canary flag in rollout controller.
- Apply routing patch to move Orion account to stable config. (routing-change.patch attached).
- Monitor p95/p99 for the next 30 minutes; if stable, confirm with Orion and close.

Policy note: because Orion is in committed capacity (deal O-9812), we should consider an SLA credit conversation depending on MTTI. I'll prep the credit calc for leadership.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Product Manager, Hosting & Deployments

Attachments: routing-change.patch (diff, 2KB)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Collins <jamie@orionai.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 10:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: (URGENT) Hosted API latency spike after canary

Jamie — we propose to pause the canary for Orion and route your traffic back to v2.0-stable while the runtime team investigates.

Plan and timing:
- Pause canary and swap routing: ASAP, target within 20–30 minutes.
- Post-swap: monitor p95/p99 for 60 minutes and share dashboards.
- Follow-up: postmortem and a summary of corrective work.

If you approve, we will proceed immediately and keep you updated every 30 minutes until it stabilizes.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Collins <jamie@orionai.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Sep 2026 15:42:10 -0000
Subject: Executive summary: Orion latency incident (canary rollback + next steps)

Team — final note for leadership and Orion:
- Timeline: canary v2.1 rolled 2026-09-05T01:35Z; Orion reported anomalies 08:12Z; canary paused and Orion routed to v2.0-stable 2026-09-05T11:20Z.
- Customer impact: p95 elevated for ~2.5 hours for Orion (observed increase from ~230ms to ~1.6s). Several requests hit client-side timeouts causing retries.
- Remediation: successful pause and routing swap; Orion p95/p99 returned to baseline within 25 minutes post-swap.
- Root cause (preliminary): new attention kernel in v2.1-canary changed memory access patterns causing intermittent KV cache fragmentation on long-context requests.
- Next steps:
  1) Marcus to continue kernel-level profiling and create a reproducible test case (owner: Marcus, ETA 3 business days).
  2) Priyom to schedule an internal rollback decision window and update rollout gating to require longer tail-latency trials before canary promotion (owner: Priyom, ETA 5 business days).
  3) Product & Sales to prepare customer-facing postmortem and SLA credit proposal (owner: Connor & Marissa, ETA 2 business days).
  4) Engineering to add a routing safeguard for long-context requests during kernel experiments (owner: Aditya, ETA 7 business days).

Action items are entered as SRE-4123; I've linked the incident dashboard and the profiling artifacts for all. We will provide Orion with a clear postmortem and the credit calc within 48 hours.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
